text.p: Allegiance Healthcare Corp said Thursday it signed a five year agreement under which General Medical Corp will distribute Allegiance Healthcare products to hospital and non-hospital customers.
The agreement is expected to produce sales of more than $100 million for the companies, according to a joint statement.
Allegiance Healthcare is currently part of Baxter International Inc. It will be the U.S. operating subsidiary of Allegiance Corp, which will spin off at the end of this month from Baxter.

General Medical, a privately-held company based in Richmond, Va., distributes medical supplies, equipment and services to hospitals and non-hospital sites including physician offices, clinics and surgery centers. It had 1995 sales of $1.5 billion.
Both companies expect to benefit from the agreement.

With cost pressures in health care causing more patients to be treated in lower-cost settings outside hospitals, Allegiance said one of its strategies is to increase sales of its products to surgery centers, physician offices, clinics and other alternate-site health-care providers.
General Medical said the pact will provide more product offerings for its customers.
